newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI STOCKS SEEN UP SLIGHTLY ON IMF LOAN PACKAGE.
newsitem.headline: THAI STOCKS SEEN UP SLIGHTLY ON IMF LOAN PACKAGE.

text.p: The Thai stock market was expected to gain slightly on Wednesday on reports that the IMF and several nations pledged to provide some $16 billion to help ease Thailand's economic problems, brokers said.
"The loans to be given by IMF and other countries should improve Thailand's economy in future. This is good news and should make the market rise today," said Padermpob Songkroh of Nava Finance.
The composite SET index finished off 4.60 points at 632.25 on thin 2.82 billion baht turnover on Monday. The market was closed on Tuesday for Queen Sirikit's birthday.
Brokers said investors were waiting for conditions to be laid out by the IMF after the agency agreed to provide loans to Thailand on Monday.

"Investors are also waiting to see whether the government would cut personal income and corporate taxes to ease the people's burden following an increase of the value added tax (VAT)," Padermpob said.
The VAT will be hiked to 10 from seven percent from this Saturday.
